name: Maputo
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Maputo: port and corridor partners, government counterparties, CACM arbitration support and asset research.
hero_lede: Maputo is Mozambique's capital, its main port and the seat of national government, banking and arbitration. TDSC scopes investigative consulting from Nashville for Maputo matters, working from lawful sources and coordinating qualified Mozambican professionals and counsel where local enquiries or record retrieval are required.
intro: Maputo is the capital and largest city of Mozambique, with 1,088,449 residents at the 2017 census, and it is administered as a province of its own, separate from the surrounding Maputo Province. The wider urban area, including the neighbouring city of Matola, holds well over two million people. The city's economy rests on commerce, government and the port, which handled about 30.9 million tonnes of cargo in 2024 and exports coal, chrome, magnetite, sugar and timber from Mozambique and its inland neighbours. Light manufacturing, construction, aluminium smelting in the Matola area and a services sector built around ministries, banks, donors and international agencies complete the picture.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Maputo because decisions about Mozambique's large projects are taken there, even when the assets lie in Cabo Delgado, Tete or the central corridors. Ministries, state-owned enterprises, licensing authorities and the main banks are concentrated in the capital, and so are the intermediaries who connect foreign investors with them. The Maputo Corridor links the port to South Africa and Eswatini, drawing freight agents, terminal operators and trading companies with cross-border structures. The legacy of the 2016 undisclosed state-guaranteed loans also means that lenders and investors scrutinise government-linked counterparties in the city with particular care.

matters.title: Port and corridor counterparties
matters.text: Freight forwarders, clearing agents, terminal service providers and trucking firms on the Maputo Corridor often operate through related companies on both sides of the Ressano Garcia border. We map ownership and affiliations across Mozambican and South African records and look for customs, integrity and sanctions concerns before contracts are signed.

matters.title: Government-linked partners and intermediaries
matters.text: Ministries and state-owned enterprises sit in Maputo, and so do the agents who broker access to them. We research local partners and consultants for links to politically exposed persons, procurement disputes and earlier corruption allegations, so clients can judge whether a proposed relationship can be defended to lenders and regulators.

matters.title: Banking and lender due diligence
matters.text: Mozambique's banks and financial institutions are headquartered in the capital. For lenders, development finance institutions and investors we review the principals, shareholders and litigation histories of Maputo borrowers and sponsors, and the media and court record around state-guaranteed borrowing since the 2016 hidden-debt revelations.

matters.title: Arbitration and dispute support
matters.text: Commercial disputes involving Mozambican parties are often referred to arbitration seated in Maputo or abroad. We support counsel with corporate histories, witness backgrounds and asset research on opposing parties, scoped to the procedural stage and to what lawful public sources in Mozambique can show.

matters.title: Real estate and urban development
matters.text: Construction, hotel and housing projects in Maputo and Matola attract foreign capital and local partners whose land-use rights and ownership may be hard to confirm. We research the companies, principals and disputes behind a project, with local professionals retrieving cadastre and registry documents where required.

local_context.title: Courts sitting in Maputo
local_context.text: Maputo hosts the Supreme Court and the country's other senior courts, and as a province it has its own provincial-level judicial court, which hears larger civil and commercial claims at first instance. Commercial litigation in Mozambique tends to be slow, and practitioners report that cases can take years to conclude. Counsel will advise on which court and section has jurisdiction for a given dispute, and our research is shaped around that forum and its document requirements.

local_context.title: CACM arbitration centre
local_context.text: The Centre for Arbitration, Conciliation and Mediation (CACM) is based in Maputo, with a delegation in Beira, and has long been described as the country's principal arbitral institution. Arbitration is governed by Law no. 11/99, drawn largely from the UNCITRAL Model Law, and domestic awards are enforced through the courts in the same way as judgments. For parties choosing Maputo as a seat, CACM provides rules, administration and lists of arbitrators.

local_context.title: Port concession and corridor bodies
local_context.text: The Port of Maputo is run under concession by the Maputo Port Development Company, in which the state port and rail company CFM holds a stake alongside private partners. CFM holds interests in all of Mozambique's port concessions and operates the rail links into South Africa. Concession documents, corridor agreements and cross-border rail arrangements are relevant when reviewing logistics counterparties and the parties behind terminal and rail investments.

local_context.title: Registries and filings in the capital
local_context.text: Company records are held by the Legal Entities Registry, and incorporations and amendments are published in the Boletim da República, both administered nationally with principal offices in Maputo. In practice, certified extracts, publications and property documents for Maputo businesses are retrieved in person or through local agents. Coverage of older filings and the availability of beneficial ownership information should be confirmed for each request.

tdsc_approach: TDSC has no office in Maputo and works on Maputo matters from Nashville. We first agree the purpose with the client and its counsel, whether a port or corridor contract, a lending decision, an arbitration or an enforcement plan, and scope research to that purpose. Sources include Boletim da República publications, Legal Entities Registry extracts, court and arbitration materials made available through counsel, Portuguese-language media and records in South Africa, Portugal and Mauritius where Maputo structures often connect. Any local enquiries, document retrieval or site visits are carried out by qualified Mozambican professionals under Mozambican counsel's guidance. Reports are prepared in English, with Portuguese source documents identified and confidence levels stated.

faqs.q: Do you have an office or staff in Maputo?
faqs.a: No. TDSC works from Nashville and has no office, staff or address in Mozambique. Where an engagement needs documents retrieved in Maputo, interviews or a site visit, we coordinate qualified local professionals and work with Mozambican counsel, who confirms what each activity requires under local law before it begins.

faqs.q: Can you support a CACM arbitration seated in Maputo?
faqs.a: Yes, as a consultant to the party's counsel. We prepare background research on opposing parties and witnesses, reconstruct corporate histories from Boletim da República publications and registry extracts, and identify assets that may matter for enforcement. We do not act as counsel and do not give legal advice on the arbitration itself.

faqs.q: How do you check a freight or clearing agent on the Maputo Corridor?
faqs.a: We identify the company's shareholders and directors from Mozambican records, check for related companies in South Africa and Eswatini, and review litigation, media coverage, customs-related allegations and sanctions exposure. The aim is to confirm who controls the business and whether integrity problems have been reported before goods or payments move through it.

faqs.q: Are records for Maputo companies available online?
faqs.a: Partly. Some publications and registry information can be consulted remotely, but certified extracts, older filings and property documents are usually obtained in person in Maputo through local agents. Portuguese is the language of the records, and timescales vary, so we build retrieval time into the scope rather than relying solely on online searches.

faqs.q: Why is government-linked diligence emphasised for Maputo?
faqs.a: Ministries, state-owned enterprises and licensing bodies are concentrated in the capital, and the 2016 revelations about undisclosed state-guaranteed loans made lenders and investors more cautious about government-linked counterparties. We look for political exposure, procurement history and public allegations so that clients can decide on safeguards before committing.

review_flags: City population is the 2017 INE census figure via Wikipedia; no current INE or World Bank city estimate was found. Metro figure deliberately vague because Wikipedia gives conflicting numbers (1.77m vs 2.72m).
Port tonnage (30.9 million tonnes, 2024) is from EBSCO; MPDC concession end date (Wikipedia says 2030) and any extension were not verified, so not stated.
Specific Maputo court names (Tribunal Judicial da Cidade de Maputo, any commercial sections) were not verified; text kept general.
Not verified from sources and therefore not stated: Bolsa de Valores de Mocambique and Banco de Mocambique details; Mozal named only generically as aluminium smelting in the Matola area.
Clifford Chance arbitration source is from 2014; check whether CACM remains the principal institution and Law 11/99 is unchanged.
